title: ERP Transfer
text: Hello everyone. In this session, we're going to dive into ERP transfers, what they are, the requirements, and how the process works. Whether your customer is considering a transfer or you just wanna understand the details, this session will cover everything you need to know. Let's get started. Here's our agenda for today. We'll begin with an overview of ERP transfers, go over the requirements, explore add-on services, walk through the process and timeline, answer some common questions, and wrap up with the ERP assist request process along with resources. An ERP transfer occurs when a customer is switching to a new ERP system or adding a new integration while managing in-progress projects.

title: ERP Transfer
text: Our ERP professional services team helps ensure these projects sync correctly with the new connector. It's important to note that this service comes with a minimum cost of eight thousand dollars USD per Procore instance. This fee includes preparation for up to fifteen projects with an additional charge of a hundred dollars USD per project beyond that. Customers moving to Viewpoint Vista should also be aware that data access limitations with Rivet may impact their transfer process. To ensure a smooth and successful ERP transfer, the following requirements must be in place before we begin the process. First, we begin by disabling the previous ERP integration.

title: ERP Transfer
text: This is a coordinated effort between the customer and the IAS team, where they both agree on a specific date for our engineers to disconnect the old integration. Next, the cost codes and cost types must align between Procore and the new ERP system. There needs to be a strict one-to-one match, no merging, splitting, or deleting of cost codes that are currently in use. Third, the project status in the new ERP must meet specific conditions. For most integrations, projects should not exist in a new ERP system prior to the transfer. However, if the new integration only supports job import, the customer will create the job manually, and ERP professional services will link it accordingly.

title: ERP Transfer
text: Finally, regarding financial data handling, the customer is responsible for exporting financial records using their integration tools. This ensures that all necessary data is available to be sent to the new ERP for the in-scope projects. Beyond the standard transfer, we also offer add-on services for customers who need additional support. Cost code reformatting is an option if a customer needs to adjust their cost structure while maintaining a one-to-one match. RAS exporting services allow customers to get expert help with exports and troubleshooting after the ERP transfer if they prefer not to manage it themselves.

title: ERP Transfer
text: For select integrations, we offer commitment and change order import services to ensure financial records are correctly synced between Procore and the ERP system. These services provide flexibility based on customer needs, but it's important to note that they come at an additional cost. If your customer is considering any of these, we can discuss pricing and scope based on their specific transfer requirements. To ensure a smooth and successful ERP transfer, the process is broken into two structured phases over four weeks, with ERP professional services work occurring in weeks one and two, and customer-led data exports taking place in weeks three and four.

title: ERP Transfer
text: We begin the process with project plan prep and review, where ERP professional services aligns with the customer on project scope and set expectations for the transfer. From there, ERP professional services takes the lead during weeks one and two. This includes auditing and confirming the project list, setting up cost codes and cost types in a new ERP system, completing the ERP connector setup. During this period, it's critical that the ERP integrations tool remain inactive. No cost code or cost type changes are made, and no new projects are created in Procore. At the end of week two, we conduct a go-live call with the IAS team.

title: ERP Transfer
text: This is an in-depth training where we walk through the new ERP integration, ensure configuration is correct, and validate that the system is functioning as expected. Then in weeks three and four, the customer is responsible for the post-data work. This includes exporting or applying subcontractor invoices in the ERP system and adding direct costs and applying payments to those invoices. Once all of this work is complete and validated, we move toward implementation closeout, the final checkpoint where we review everything with the customer and formally complete the ERP transfer implementation. Here are some of the most common questions we get. First, is ERP Core required? Yes. It must be purchased along with, with the ERP transfer service.

title: ERP Transfer
text: Next, what makes a transfer more challenging? So the biggest hurdles are pre-existing data in both systems and the inability to merge cost codes or types, which may require manual updates. How long does the transfer take? Well, typically it takes about four weeks, two weeks for audits and another two for data work. During this time, only the ERP integrations tool is unavailable while all the other Procore functions remain unchanged. And finally, what information helps with scoping? While the ISC will handle most of this, having details on the customer's ERP integration, go-live timeline, project list, and any planned cost code updates will streamline the process.

title: ERP Transfer
text: When you're ready to move forward with an ERP transfer, submitting an ERP assist request in Salesforce is the next step. This process ensures that all necessary details are captured for a smooth transfer. So first, we'll select ERP integration services as the assisting team. Under type, choose sales support. For main product, select accounting integrations. Under sub-product, select the specific ERP integration. And in the description, be sure to indicate the current ERP system and the one the customer is moving to. It's important to note that this process is specifically for ERP transfer requests.

title: ERP Transfer
text: If the customer has not received an ERP integration demo before creating the assist request, stop what you're doing and contact the solution specialist or sales engineer for the account. The demo must be completed before an integration services consultant can assist with the transfer. Additionally, please confirm in the description that your client has had a demo. This step is crucial to ensuring a seamless handoff and avoiding unnecessary delays in the process. So where do you go for resources and questions? First, your go-to hub is Highspot. It contains all relevant guides, documentation, and collateral related to ERP transfers, integrations, and services.

title: ERP Transfer
text: You can also reach out via Slack to our ERP support channel for any ERP-specific integrations. And also you have the prof_services, which is an open space to ask questions about professional services. And finally, you'll find a direct link to the assist request form in Salesforce if you're looking to kick off an ERP transfer request or need sales support to get it scoped and started. So whether you're looking for documentation or expert advice, these resources have you covered. Thank you.

title: Introduction to Procore& Sage300CRE Integration by ERP Team

Speaker: Laura Widman, Integration Specialist

Hello, my name is Laura Widman. I am an integration specialist with Procore working with the Workday connector. Today I will be going over two touch points with our feature set map. title: Introduction to ProcoreWorkday Inte

To add to Procore, you'd click on this "Add to Procore" button, and that lands the company into your synced filter here. This is now synced and ready to be used on contracts and change orders.

title: Introduction to ProcoreWorkday Inte
text: To export a contract from Procore into Workday, you would create that contract in Procore, fill out all necessary fields, and then you would click accept and export to Workday. One piece to note with looking for a contract in Workday: since it's called a supplier contract, we can look up that supplier ID right here in Workday and this contract will fall underneath that. To look that up in Workday, I would type in "supplier:" and the supplier ID. Then there's a "Contracts and Purchase Orders" tab, and here is my most recent contract. If you click into the magnifying glass, that gives you the contract number and more details like the line items. Okay.

title: Introduction to ProcoreWorkday Inte
text: Now, my change order will be ready to be sent to the ERP tab because we have an approved and synced contract. So after filling out all necessary fields, I send that commitment change order over to our ERP tool. And under that ERP tool, we have the commitment change orders tab. title: Introduction to ProcoreWorkday Inte

title: Introduction to Procore Acumatica In
text:
ntroduction to Procore_Acumatica Integration by ERP Team.md
Speaker: Allegra Sesayna, Integration Implementation Team

Hi, my name is Allegra Sesayna. I'm here with Procore's integration implementation team for our ERP integrations. And I am going to be walking you through some of the key features of the Acumatica integration. To start, let's open up our ERP tool. We'll go to financial management and we'll click ERP integrations. This will take us to the ERP staging tool, and this is where I'm going to be showing you how to sync up companies, commitments, and change orders today. Starting with companies, we do support a bidirectional workflow at the time. We will be able to export vendors as well as import vendors in from your ERP system.

title: Introduction to Procore Acumatica In
text: For the sake of today's demo, we're going to focus on bringing your existing ERP vendors into Procore's directory tool. To request vendors to pull in from your Acumatica system, you'll click the "Refresh Company List" here, and this process is what will populate the list we see in front of us. All of these are going to be vendors in our Acumatica system that we can bring into Procore. Let's choose one of these vendors to bring in. Looking at the list here, one that sticks out to me is American Insurance Company. These exist in Acumatica under the Payables tab for vendors. So if I wanted to confirm that this vendor is the one I'm looking for, I can type it in here and find American Insurance Company.

title: Introduction to Procore Acumatica In
text: Coming back to the directory tab here, let's go ahead and add this item into Procore. We're going to click the "Add to Procore" button, and we'll get a notification that this has been added to the Procore directory and is now synced with ERP. If we come back to our directory tool in Procore at the company level and refresh, we should get an updated populated list of synced vendors. And if we just scroll down to the fifth or sixth one here, we'll see the American Insurance Company is now in fact ERP synced, and it even notes the vendor ID from Acumatica. That's how you integrate companies from the Acumatica portal into the Procore portal. Now let's jump over to commitments. Commitments refers to subcontracts and purchase orders.

title: Introduction to Procore Acumatica In
text: These will go to different screen modules within Acumatica, but they can both always be found under the commitments tab of a project. So, let's go ahead and integrate a new commitment. I have one already made here—it's a subcontract. I'm going to click the "Send to ERP" button and we're going to push that to the ERP tool. I'm going to refresh the page, and we should now see my new contract is listed. It shows the SOV line items that we're going to be pushing over to the ERP system as well. And as an accounting approver, I'm now ready to push this over into the ERP system. I'm going to click "Export to Acumatica" and that's going to go ahead and push through.

title: Introduction to Procore Acumatica In
text: While we wait for that to sync, I can show you the places we can expect to find this. There is a global subcontract page where you can find all subcontracts listed across all projects along with their statuses, totals, and any relevant quantities or dates. You can also open up the project that this contract will be syncing to by going to Project. And on that project is a commitments tab. The commitments tab is where all of the subcontracts and purchase orders for this specific job will integrate. As this pushes through, we can take a step back and prepare our next item. Oh, never mind—we have a successful export. So, if I refresh this now, we'll see a fourth one has populated here with a status of open.

title: Introduction to Procore Acumatica In
text: All contracts, whether subcontracts or purchase orders, will post to the ERP system in an open status. If we wanted to open this up further and take a look just to verify the details look good, we can click on that hyperlink there and it's going to open up a window that will show us the details of this particular contract. So we'll see our two line items here for the same overall subcontract amount and retainage amount we had set from the system to the applicable vendor. Now let's push over a change order. I already have one ready to go on a previously synced contract here. We're going to go ahead and "Send to ERP." This particular change order is going to be updating an existing contract line item to add more cost.

title: Introduction to Procore Acumatica In
text: So we'll move over to our commitments tab. This is also an export-only feature and it is just like the previous tab in that there is only an accept or a reject button. As an accounting approver, I'm going to go ahead and hit accept and we're going to verify that this line item pushes over. We'll export that to Acumatica. This can be found in a few places as well. There is still a global change order tab. If we go up to change orders here, we can see all change order types across all jobs in the ERP system. This will include your contract change orders, prime contract change orders, and budget change orders as well. Contract change orders will always post with this closed status here. And we can also find them by going onto the project.

title: Introduction to Procore Acumatica In
text: So this is under the same job. I'm going to reopen my commitments tab, and we are specifically syncing a change to this item here—my previously synced contract. So I'm going to open this up, and within this particular record is another change order tab specific to just this contract. Refresh there. If we come back to the main page and we go back into our global page, we can also see the item is going to post there. And there it is, up at the top with a closed status, which means it has successfully exported from Procore. And this has the exact same interface as the commitment we just opened. Now you know how to successfully sync commitment change orders, commitments, and companies with our ERP system. Thanks for watching!

title: Introduction to Procore Netsuite In
heading: Introduction to Procore_Netsuite Integration by ERP Team
text:
**Speaker:** Megan Roshevits

Hi, this is Megan Roshevits from Procore’s ERP implementation team. Today, I’ll be walking you through some of the data pieces that integrate between Procore and NetSuite through Procore’s built ERP integration. As we walk through this brief demo today, it’s important to note that the data pieces that we’re covering are not the full functionality of the integration. You’ll cover the ERP integration’s tool in much more depth during implementation with your integration implementation specialist. So for our short demo today, we’re going to start by covering the Procore ERP integrations tool, specifically how our Procore and NetSuite vendors, subcontractor invoices, and owner invoices sync through the integration.

title: Introduction to Procore Netsuite In
heading: Introduction to Procore_Netsuite Integration by ERP Team
text: We’re going to start in Procore and we’ll also be jumping into NetSuite as well, and we’re going to begin by accessing the ERP integrations tool. The ERP integrations tool is essentially the staging area between Procore and NetSuite. So all of our data that’s going back and forth between the two systems will flow through this tool. So to access the tool, we’ll access our company tools, and then underneath financial management, we have ERP integrations. With this being the staging area and dashboard for the ERP integration, our tabs at the top are representing our syncable data pieces. As I mentioned, for our demonstration today, we’ll be covering companies, subcontractor invoices, and owner invoices.

title: Introduction to Procore Netsuite In
heading: Introduction to Procore_Netsuite Integration by ERP Team
text: So beginning with companies, in this tab, I first want to draw our attention to the right side of the screen, which are these filters. The filters are essentially a way that Procore is sorting your data based on what currently exists in NetSuite and is eligible to be imported into Procore. That will always be the "Ready to Import" filter. So currently in my companies tab, I have 77 AP vendors in NetSuite that are staged in, available to add to my Procore directory if I choose to do so. The second filter, "Ready to Export," is if we’re moving the other direction with our data. So if I’ve created an AP vendor in Procore and I want to export it out to NetSuite, that would flow through the "Ready to Export" filter.

title: Introduction to Procore Netsuite In
heading: Introduction to Procore_Netsuite Integration by ERP Team
text: So the vendors are a bidirectional sync, meaning you’ll want to pick a workflow of either originating AP vendors in Procore and sending them out to NetSuite, or setting up AP vendors in NetSuite and importing into Procore. For this integration, it is a more common workflow to import our vendors from our ERP system. So we’re going to show an example today of a vendor that’s been created in NetSuite and how we can add that into our Procore directory to use on our contracts with the integration. So I’m going to jump over to the NetSuite side just briefly and take a look at an AP vendor that I’ve recently created.

title: Introduction to Procore Netsuite In
heading: Introduction to Procore_Netsuite Integration by ERP Team
text: When we’re originating our AP vendors in NetSuite, all we have to do on the NetSuite side is create the vendor by adding the required information and then save. Once we’ve saved the vendor, once a day the integration will pick up any newly created vendors and add them into our "Ready to Import" filter. So of these 77 vendors, I want to decide: do I want to use these in Procore? And for the NetSuite integration specifically, what we want to consider is from these 77 vendors, which of these will I definitely be using on subcontracts and purchase orders? Those will absolutely be the vendors we want to add to Procore. Additionally, we’ll want to add any vendors to Procore that might have a direct cost associated on the NetSuite side.

title: Introduction to Procore Netsuite In
heading: Introduction to Procore_Netsuite Integration by ERP Team
text: We’ll want to go ahead and sync those vendors in our Procore directory as well. So when we’re importing a vendor from NetSuite into Procore, what I’m going to do is just search my "Ready to Import" for the vendor that I created: HP Corporation. So there it is, and moving left to right, you can see that I have three different options. The first option is "Link to existing company." This hyperlink will search your Procore directory for an exact name match of HP Corporation to see if it already exists in our Procore directory. If it does already exist in our Procore directory, that means that somebody has already created it in Procore as a company.

title: Introduction to Procore Netsuite In
heading: Introduction to Procore_Netsuite Integration by ERP Team
text: So in this case, instead of clicking "Add to Procore," I’m going to select the name match that the vendor found and select "Link" to add those into my Procore directory. So now I’ve linked my Procore version of the company to my NetSuite version, and my synced filter will go up by one. The synced filter indicates the record exists in both systems and is one but synced together. So I can see there is HP Corporation. So when I open that up in a new tab, we’ll take a look at a few items that will be different for a synced vendor versus a non-synced vendor. The first thing we’ll point out is this green "ERP Synced" banner. This will be applicable for our jobs and invoices as well. Anything that’s synced with NetSuite will have the green banner.

title: Introduction to Procore Netsuite In
heading: Introduction to Procore_Netsuite Integration by ERP Team
text: And then additionally, this ERP Vendor ID of 902—this is just the NetSuite vendor ID number saying this vendor is now linked to this Procore company. So now, in theory, I could create a subcontract in Procore and use HP Corporation as my contract company, and then when I invoice that commitment, I would be able to send that invoice to NetSuite. So our contract company on our invoices is required to be an ERP synced vendor. And now that we’ve covered importing a vendor, let’s move back into the ERP integrations tool and talk about subcontractor and owner invoicing.

title: Introduction to Procore Netsuite In
heading: Introduction to Procore_Netsuite Integration by ERP Team
text: So for this integration, our subcontractor and our owner invoices will be created in Procore, and once they’re in a status of approved is when they can be sent to the ERP integrations tool, our staging area, for an accounting approver to approve or reject before they’re actually sent to your accounting system. So let’s walk through an example of sending a subcontractor invoice to the ERP integrations tool, exporting that invoice to NetSuite, and then looking at the vendor bill that generates from that synced invoice. So for this example, I’m just going to open up one of my demo projects that I have a subcontractor invoice recently created. So I’ll head into my invoicing tool, which shows my subcontractor and owner invoices.

title: Introduction to Procore Netsuite In
heading: Introduction to Procore_Netsuite Integration by ERP Team
text: So we’ll enter subcontractor, and then I’ll select my most recently created invoice. A couple of items to note as you’re creating invoices to sync with the integration: one is the billing period. So our billing period for our Procore invoices are required to match our NetSuite accounting periods. So for this integration, we’ll want all our billing periods to be set up as month start to month end. And then the billing date also needs to be within that period. Outside of that, I have my schedule of values below at the bottom with my cost code and cost type. And then I’ve also gone ahead and approved this invoice, meaning I’m ready to send it to the ERP integrations tool.

title: Introduction to Procore Netsuite In
heading: Introduction to Procore_Netsuite Integration by ERP Team
text: So selecting "Send to ERP" is just simply going to land it in my subcontractor invoice tab in my "Ready to Export" filter. So here’s the invoice that I just sent to ERP. And now the accounting approver is responsible for approving or rejecting this item before it’s actually exported to NetSuite. So in this case, I’m ready to go ahead and approve, so I’ll select my invoice, click "Export," and then we’ll take a look at the vendor bill that generates once this is synced over. All right, and now that our invoice has successfully synced over, let’s jump over to NetSuite and take a look at the vendor bill. So first and foremost, we have our invoice number at the top and then our generic information from Procore.

title: Introduction to Procore Netsuite In
heading: Introduction to Procore_Netsuite Integration by ERP Team
text: And then the key importance of the integration is going to be down at the bottom in the items section. So our first item that populated is our cost code and cost type from our Procore invoice schedule of values. So the item that generates will be project specific: so my project number 2325, division 8, cost code 100, materials. So that was doors materials. And then my second line will account for any retainage. So during implementation, we will ask that the client specify an AP retainage item that our subcontractor invoice retainage defaults to. We need an item name and also an account specified, and this is set up in the integration configuration during implementation, so all AP retainage is defaulted to the correct item and account.

title: Introduction to Procore Netsuite In
heading: Introduction to Procore_Netsuite Integration by ERP Team
text: So that’s our example of syncing a subcontractor invoice and what you’ll see within the items field on the NetSuite side. Now let’s jump back over to Procore and go through the process of syncing an owner invoice with NetSuite and then looking at the invoice that generates on the NetSuite side. We will jump back into the demonstration project we’ve been using, and in my project tools, I’ll go back to my invoicing tool. And this time I’m going to select my owner invoice tab. And down at the bottom, I have my most recently created owner invoice, and we’ll open that up. The same rules apply to syncing an owner invoice as a subcontractor invoice when it comes to our billing periods.

title: Introduction to Procore Netsuite In
heading: Introduction to Procore_Netsuite Integration by ERP Team
text: Once again, our billing periods need to match our NetSuite accounting periods, and then our billing date needs to be within that period. One additional item important to note when it comes to owner invoice syncing is if we are syncing our owner invoices from Procore, the project in NetSuite is required to have a customer assigned to it. So the customer field on the project record does have to be populated in order for our Procore invoices to default the client or customer. Once we’ve verified that we have all of our required information, we’ll once again send to ERP. We will jump back into our ERP integrations tool and this time select the owner invoices tab. In my "Ready to Export" filter, I can see my invoice that I just sent.

title: Introduction to Procore Netsuite In
heading: Introduction to Procore_Netsuite Integration by ERP Team
text: Once again, the accounting approvers can reject or accept. I’ll go ahead and accept the export, and then once this is successfully synced, we will look at the invoice on the NetSuite side. Okay, our owner invoice has successfully exported, so let’s jump over to NetSuite and take a look at the invoice. Once again, we have our invoice number and our general information at the top. And then the item section is once again where the integration comes into play, but our item section will be just a little bit different when syncing an owner invoice than what we saw with a subcontractor invoice. The subcontractor invoice will have each cost code and cost type specified on its own line item.

title: Introduction to Procore Netsuite In
heading: Introduction to Procore_Netsuite Integration by ERP Team
text: For owner invoicing, all line items from your Procore owner invoice will summarize into one item in NetSuite. This also is an item that we ask the client to specify during implementation. We just need the item name and then an associated income or revenue account for all owner invoices to summarize to that item. And very similarly to what we saw with our AP retainage, any retainage on an owner invoice will also default to one item, also specified by the client, where we once again need to add the item name and associated account into our integration configuration. So now that we’ve walked through an example of vendor syncing, subcontractor syncing, and owner invoice syncing, that concludes the demo for today.

title: Introduction to Procore Netsuite In
heading: Introduction to Procore_Netsuite Integration by ERP Team
text: As I mentioned, there are many other details you’ll be covering with your implementation specialist during ERP implementation. If you’d like to check out more information about the Procore built NetSuite integration, head over to our Procore site for the Project Financials NetSuite "Things to Know" article. This is incredibly informative and we have a handful of other tutorials and walkthroughs to give you a better idea of how the integration might be able to work for you. Thank you so much for your time and we hope to work with you soon.

title: Introduction to Procore QB Desktop
text:
Introduction to Procore_QB Desktop Integration by ERP Team.md
Speaker: Bri Young, Implementation Specialist

Hi, my name is Bri and I am one of the integration implementation specialists here at Procore. Today I'm going to be showcasing some of the features of our QuickBooks Desktop integration, specifically how data flows between Procore and QuickBooks Desktop. Throughout this presentation, I will be showcasing both my demo Procore instance as well as my demo QuickBooks company file, so you will see me kind of bounce back and forth between the two different softwares.

title: Introduction to Procore QB Desktop
text: Right now I am just here on our main Procore portfolio page, and the tool that we are focusing on is our ERP integrations tool, which just lives up here under our company tools in the financial management column. Now, our ERP integration tool can be thought of as a giant staging area. So the data that is going to flow back and forth between Procore and QuickBooks Desktop will ultimately pass through this staging area, and we have accounting approvers set in place that will get the final say in the data that actually is allowed to show up in QuickBooks. So I'm going to be covering some of these tabs up here today and just kind of showing you how the data flows, what it looks like when it's in QuickBooks after export, things like that.

title: Introduction to Procore QB Desktop
text: So the first thing I'm going to focus on is going to be companies. Now, companies in our Procore directory are going to relate to vendors in our QuickBooks vendor center. So when it comes to companies, they can be synced on a bidirectional functionality. So the vendors can either be created in our Procore directory first and they can be exported out to QuickBooks, or they can be created in QuickBooks first and imported into Procore. The workflow that I'm going to be showing you today is going to be how to create a vendor in QuickBooks and get that imported over into our Procore directory. So I'm going to bring up my QuickBooks and the vendor that we're going to be focusing on is going to be Johnson Concrete.

title: Introduction to Procore QB Desktop
text: So this is a new vendor that I have just recently put into my QuickBooks vendor center. We click into them, you can see I've got their information filled in the way that I want it to be. And coming back into Procore, if I were to go over into my Procore directory and go into companies, we would see that Johnson Concrete does not exist yet. So the first thing that I'm going to want to do is I'm going to want to make sure I'm on this "Ready to Import" filter. This is the filter that is going to be in charge of importing those vendors from QuickBooks into Procore.

title: Introduction to Procore QB Desktop
text: So what I'm going to do is I'm going to hit this "Refresh Company List." That is going to trigger a manual refresh of the integration and it's going to go and search QuickBooks for any new vendors that may have been inputted into QuickBooks. Now, on the QuickBooks side, I'm just going to make sure that my web connector is up and running. I do have my web connector set up to auto-run every five minutes, so every five minutes this is running and any new requests from Procore would be processed. However, just to speed things along, I'm going to go ahead and hit "Update Selected." That's going to get things moving at a little bit faster pace here, we don't have to wait for that five-minute auto-run.

title: Introduction to Procore QB Desktop
text: All right, we can see we've got a completed status here, and we've got a successful refresh here. From there, I'm going to go ahead and just refresh my page. And we can see Johnson Concrete has pulled in at the top of our list. We also get a nice little timestamp that shows us when the last manual sync was ran. Now there is an auto-sync that is happening on an hourly basis, however, I wanted to run this right here, right now, so that's why I did this Refresh Company List option. Now, to get this vendor into my Procore directory, all I need to do is hit this "Add to Procore" button. That's going to pull them in and set them up as a new vendor in my directory.

title: Introduction to Procore QB Desktop

title: Introduction to Procore Sage 100 Co
text:
Introduction to Procore_Sage 100 Contractor Integration by ERP Team.md
Speaker: Megan, Procore ERP Team

Hello everybody. This is Megan from Procore's ERP team. Today I'm going to walk you through moving data between Procore and your ERP system, and in this case, particularly the Sage 100 Contractor system. What we're going to start with is sending a vendor from Sage 100 over to Procore. Please keep in mind that this is only one way of moving data between the systems. For a lot of our data pieces, vendors included, we can actually do a bidirectional sync, meaning that the vendor can be created in Sage 100 and imported into Procore, or you can also set up your AP vendor as a company in Procore and export it to Sage 100.

title: Introduction to Procore Sage 100 Co
text: What we'll be focusing on today is showing you a vendor that was created in Sage 100 Contractor and how we can import that vendor into Procore. So we're going to start inside Sage 100 Contractor and I'm going to open up my AP vendors. Going to select my master drop-down so I can view a list of all of my AP vendors. And from here my first goal is to locate the vendor that I created that I would like to import into Procore. So that was number 42, Grant & Knight Construction. So now that I've created my vendor and I've added my generic information, my name, my address, and I've saved this vendor record, what's going to take place now is this vendor will actually automatically stage for me inside Procore inside my ERP integrations tool.

title: Introduction to Procore Sage 100 Co
text: It's important to note the ERP integrations tool is a staging area between the ERP system and Procore, and all of our data that we're syncing back and forth does have to flow through that tool. So before we actually import Grant & Knight into our Procore directory, I'm going to take us into Procore and just double-check that my Grant & Knight does not already exist in Procore before I want to import it. So to check on that I'm just going to access my company-level directory, and inside my companies tab I'm just going to search for the first couple letters of the name of my vendor. Looks like I didn't get any search records returned, so that ensures to me that Grant & Knight does not exist in Procore.

title: Introduction to Procore Sage 100 Co
text: So I'm ready to move on to my next step to get it added to my directory. Next I'm going to access my company-level tool, ERP Integrations. And we're going to start in the companies tab. Now that I have created that vendor in Sage 100, it will automatically stage for me inside the ERP tool under my companies tab inside my filter called "Ready to Import." It's important to note these filters are sorting our data based on what currently exists in Sage and is eligible to be imported into Procore—that will be the Ready to Import filter. And then our Ready to Export filter would be if we were moving the other direction and creating a vendor in Procore that we would like to send to Sage 100.

title: Introduction to Procore Sage 100 Co
text:
So for the purpose of this example, we will focus on the Ready to Import filter. From here I can see that I have 96 vendors in Sage 100 that are eligible to be imported into Procore. So my next step is going to be to locate the vendor that I created in Sage 100 and then add it to my Procore directory. So I do have my Ready to Import sorted alphabetically at this time, so I'm just going to scroll down. I can see Grant & Knight Construction, Sage ID number 42, that is correct. So in order to now add this to my Procore directory, all I have to do is select "Add to Procore."

This will provide us with a success message saying this vendor has been added to your Procore directory.

title: Introduction to Procore Sage 100 Co
text: Additionally, that will take my synced filter up by one, indicating this is now a synced vendor. So I'm going to scroll down to my Grant & Knight—we'll go to page two here—all right, and there it is. And if I open up this synced vendor in a new tab just to view a couple of items that you'll notice once you start syncing data: first and foremost, our synced data will have this green "ERP Synced" banner, indicating the record exists in both systems and they are synced together. This will be applicable for jobs, commitments, and commitment change orders as well. And then additionally we have this external ID, this 42. This is simply the Sage vendor ID number indicating that this Procore company is now linked to this Sage vendor.

title: Introduction to Procore Sage 100 Co
text: So now in theory I could create a subcontract with Grant & Knight Construction as my contract company, and that subcontract would now be eligible to sync with Sage because I have a synced vendor. Now that we've covered importing a vendor, the next topic I would like to discuss is exporting a subcontract or a commitment and exporting a commitment change order. So I am going to open up one of my test projects here. And within my test project I'm going to access the commitments tool, which is my project-level tool under financial management. And inside my commitments tool there are going to be a couple of ERP indicators.

title: Introduction to Procore Sage 100 Co
text: So first and foremost, this column that says ERP status will let you know if the commitment is ready to be sent to the ERP integrations tool, if it's not ready—meaning there are requirements that have not been completed—or if the commitment is already synced. So I'm going to go ahead and open up this subcontract. And we will actually send this subcontract to the ERP integrations tool to then export to Sage 100. So my requirements for exporting a subcontract are going to include a unique contract number. So we do want to make sure that this identifier is completely unique because this contract number is what Sage will read as the subcontract identifier.

title: Introduction to Procore Sage 100 Co
text: I typically recommend adding the project number either leading or trailing your subcontract number just to ensure that all of our IDs are entirely unique. I'll go ahead and add my leading number. I have my title; my status does need to be approved. And then the only other requirement I have is I do have to add at least one SOV line item. So I'll go ahead and make one for us. And then once that commitment is saved and all of our requirements are met, that's when you'll be able to see this "Send to ERP" button at the top right. And selecting this button does not automatically start exporting the contract to Sage 100, but it's simply going to stage it for us in the ERP integrations tool as a Ready to Export commitment.

title: Introduction to Procore Sage 100 Co
text: So taking us back to the ERP tool in my commitments tab, I can see my corresponding project as well as the contract that I just created. And now viewing my commitment details, once an accounting approver reviews these details, we are eligible to accept the export. Now once we click "Export to Sage 100," it will take a few minutes to actually create the subcontract in Sage 100. So the next item we're going to cover is when the subcontract is exported to Sage 100, where does that land inside Sage 100 Contractor and what does it look like? So now that I can see that my subcontract successfully exported, now we want to take a look in Sage 100 to see where that landed at.

title: Introduction to Procore Sage 100 Co
text: So I'm going to open up Sage 100 Contractor again and access menu 6-7-1 Subcontracts. And then once that opens up, I'm just going to go to my most recent subcontract, which should be the most recent one that I synced. And there it is from Procore: the exact commitment that I created. I have my subcontract number, my description, my single line schedule of values, and my dates populated as well. So now with a synced subcontract, we are able to invoice this in either Sage or Procore. And now that we've discussed a subcontract syncing, the last piece that I'd like to talk about today is going to be syncing a commitment change order.

title: Introduction to Procore Sage 100 Co
text: So we are going to go back to Procore and I'm going to select again another demonstration project that we have with a commitment change order to walk us through the steps of how that gets exported to Sage 100 and what we'll see in that system. So I'm going to open up my change orders tool and then underneath the commitments tab I should be able to see any of my commitment change orders that I've created up to this point. So I do have one that is available to view. So I do have a commitment change order here that is ready to be sent to the ERP tool. The requirements for sending a commitment change order to the ERP tool are very similar to what we saw with syncing a subcontract.

title: Introduction to Procore Sage 100 Co
text: We do have to have a change order number, a title, as well as one line of schedule of values. And then once our commitment change order is also in a status of approved, that is when it's eligible to be sent again to the ERP tool for an accounting approver to review. So if I select "Send to ERP," I will take us back to our ERP integrations tool where that commitment change order should be waiting for us. So I'll select my commitment change orders, Ready to Export, and I can see here is my CCO that I created and sent to ERP. So once again, the role of the accounting approver is to review and accept before exporting to Sage 100.

title: Introduction to Procore Sage 100 Co
text: Once we click export, we will receive a message to let you know please make sure that the subcontract that the change order is against is not currently open in Sage 100. So just a cautionary message to confirm. And then once again we'll get the exporting, please be patient, this may take a few minutes. title: Introduction to Procore Viewpoint V
heading: Introduction to Procore_Viewpoint Vista Integration by ERP Team
text:
**Speaker:** Jeff Wright

Hi everybody, this is Jeff Wright from Procore’s ERP team. Today I’m going to walk you through moving data between Procore and your ERP system, in this case particularly the Viewpoint Vista ERP system. What we’re going to do is start with sending a vendor from Vista over to Procore. Please keep in mind that this is only one way of moving data between the systems. For a lot of objects, vendors included, we can do a bidirectional sync, which means that the vendor can be created in Vista and moved into Procore, or you can go ahead and set up the vendor on the Procore side and export it to Vista. What I’m going to be showing you today is a vendor that is in Vista and how we can get that over to Procore.

title: Introduction to Procore Viewpoint V
heading: Introduction to Procore_Viewpoint Vista Integration by ERP Team
text: So, we’re going to start in Vista. We’ll go to programs, AP vendors, and I’m going to go ahead and search for the vendor that I want to bring over, which is the vendor called Big Time Demolition. So I’ll go ahead and search for that and we’ll go ahead and bring up the vendor record here in Vista. Before I do anything else, I’m going to just pop back to Procore and what I’m going to show you here is the company directory. And really you can see all the vendors that we have; we do not have Big Time Demolition on the list. I’ll go ahead and search for it and you can see it is not currently in Procore. So to bring a vendor over—kind of backing up—any data entered into Vista syncs back to Procore on an hourly basis.

title: Introduction to Procore Viewpoint V
heading: Introduction to Procore_Viewpoint Vista Integration by ERP Team
text: And it doesn’t automatically just, like for example, a vendor won’t automatically just come into the company directory. What it’s going to do is it’s going to land in the ERP tool in Procore. The ERP tool is a company-level tool, and here we are. I’m on the companies tab and what I’ve done here is I’ve got a whole list of all of the active vendors that are in Vista. So again, these have not been added to kind of Procore proper yet; they’re not in the company directory. They’re just waiting to be added, sitting here in this "Ready to Import" filter, essentially as a record that is staged and is able to be added to Procore.

title: Introduction to Procore Viewpoint V
heading: Introduction to Procore_Viewpoint Vista Integration by ERP Team
text: Like I said, if this vendor had—this vendor itself was already in Vista, but if I just entered a brand new vendor right now, what would happen is it would get pulled into this ERP tool when the hourly sync between Vista and Procore runs. Just to clarify, data entered in Procore—and I’ll show you a little bit of this later—will be exported to Vista, and that essentially happens in real time. So, data exported from Procore to Vista happens on demand; data entered in Vista will sync back to Procore on an hourly basis. Okay, so we’re going to go ahead and search for this vendor in my list here. Just go ahead and search. Okay, so here we go, we’ve got Big Time Demolition. Again, you can see that it’s brought over some basic vendor information.

title: Introduction to Procore Viewpoint V
heading: Introduction to Procore_Viewpoint Vista Integration by ERP Team
text: We’ve also got the vendor ID number—that’s kind of key because that’s really what’s going to link the vendor between the two systems is that vendor ID. And to bring it into Procore, all you have to do is go ahead and click this "Add to Procore" button. You’ll see that it’s been added to the Procore directory. We will hop back over to the directory, go ahead and refresh my screen, and here we are: we’ve got Big Time Demolition now in the Procore company directory. Okay, so what we’re going to do next is I’m going to go ahead and show you how to send data from Procore over to Vista. Specifically, what we’re going to look at is going to be sending a commitment, a subcontract, and then we’ll go ahead and send over a commitment change order.

title: Introduction to Procore Viewpoint V
heading: Introduction to Procore_Viewpoint Vista Integration by ERP Team
text: Okay, back over here in Procore, what I’ve done is I’ve navigated to one of my demo projects, this project 115978, and what you’re looking at here is the project tools and the list of commitments. And what I wanted to show you here is that we’ve got three subcontracts that are currently synced with Vista. So they were sent through the integration over to the Vista side. And then I’ve got one more subcontract that I’m going to be getting ready to send here for my demo. What I’m going to do over on the Vista side is let’s go down to the subcontract ledger module. That’s where your subcontracts are going to end up when they’re exported. Purchase orders—we’ll go to the PO module.

title: Introduction to Procore Viewpoint V
heading: Introduction to Procore_Viewpoint Vista Integration by ERP Team
text: We’ll go ahead to subcontract ledger and what I think I’m going to do is go ahead and show you the report here. It’s the SL Subcontract Ledger Report. It’s a good way to look at the data that’s been sent over from Procore to Vista. I’ve got the report launcher pulled up here and we’ll go ahead and preview this. And really what I’m going to show you here is just we’ve got, as you can see on my list here, we’ve got subcontract 1 over in Vista, we’ve got subcontract 2, and we’ve got subcontract 3. And then if we go to the summary page, you’ll see that is all the subcontracts. And so what I’m going to do now is take this subcontract that has already been set up in Procore.

title: Introduction to Procore Viewpoint V
heading: Introduction to Procore_Viewpoint Vista Integration by ERP Team
text: Two of the main things I wanted to point out here too is that before you can send the subcontract, the status on the subcontract has to be approved and your contract company has to be synced with Vista. So this would be the kind of process we worked through previously where we imported a vendor from Vista and you can see that it has an associated vendor ID. And so now I’m going to come up here, click on the "Send to ERP" button. So this isn’t going to send it automatically to Vista, but it is going to send it over to the ERP tool. And I’ll jump over to the commitments tab, and then we’ve got our "Ready to Export" filter, and then we’ve got our approved metals subcontract here. You can see that the batch date is going to default to today.

title: Introduction to Procore Viewpoint V
heading: Introduction to Procore_Viewpoint Vista Integration by ERP Team
text: If you do need to change that, say you need to send it in a prior month, you can change the date on that. And then as an accounting approver—these are the people responsible for sending data from Procore to Vista—you would click the "Accept" button. Optionally, if you do want to apply a compliance group, you can do that here. Go ahead and pick that, and then you’ll go ahead and click the "Export to Vista" button. This generally takes, I would say, about a minute or so before it fully goes through. So we’ll actually just kind of sit here, wait for this to happen in real time.

title: Introduction to Procore Viewpoint V
heading: Introduction to Procore_Viewpoint Vista Integration by ERP Team
text: And if there is some kind of problem with the export when it goes to Vista—say maybe, I don’t think it’s going to be the case, but if that accounting month was closed, we wouldn’t be able to add the subcontract to Vista, and what would happen is we’d get an error message in Procore telling us what the problem is and then the export would fall into this "Failed to Export" filter. That way you know that, you know, first of all you don’t have to sit here and just watch this every time you send something. You can kind of let it run and then if there is a failure, you’ll get that error message and it’ll drop down into that failed to export filter so you can go in and fix whatever the issue was.

title: Introduction to Procore Viewpoint V
heading: Introduction to Procore_Viewpoint Vista Integration by ERP Team
text: The other thing I wanted to mention while we’re waiting for this to export is that things like subcontracts and change orders are kind of—they go through a batch posting process in Vista. When we export data from Procore to Vista, we actually send these objects through the batch posting process. So when this gets over to Vista, this will have been fully posted. So you do not need to take any further action on the Vista side once this is finished exporting. So if you wanted to, you could actually go into Vista and pull up the batch that this was sent over in and take a look at the line item data, or you can go in—what I’m going to do—and look at the export on the SL Subcontract Ledger Report.

title: Introduction to Procore Viewpoint V
heading: Introduction to Procore_Viewpoint Vista Integration by ERP Team
text: Okay, so we can see that it was successfully exported. Hop back over to my Vista report launcher, go ahead and click the "Preview" button. Okay, so now we’ve got subcontract 1, 2, and 3, which were already there, and now we’ve got subcontract 4. And if we kind of looked previously at the commitment over on the Procore side—go ahead and refresh—yeah, just a simple contract. You can see that it has the synced banner on it. The schedule of values is $50,000 to this metal subcontractor cost code, and that is what we also see over here on the Vista side. Okay, and so the last thing I’m going to do is I’m going to show you what it would look like to send over a subcontract change order on this same subcontract.

title: Introduction to Procore Viewpoint V
heading: Introduction to Procore_Viewpoint Vista Integration by ERP Team
text: And we’ll kind of go through the same exercise where we will go ahead, create the commitment change order in Procore, it’ll be added to this commitment, we’ll go ahead and send it through the connector, and then we’ll run this report and you’ll be able to see that the subcontract now has that change order associated with it over on the Vista side. Okay, so I’m going to go ahead and close out my subcontract ledger report. And we’re back at our in Procore—we’ve got our contract. And what we can see now is that we’ve got our original contract value of $50,000 and we’ve got a draft change order for $10,000. So we’ll go ahead, hop over to the change orders tab, go ahead and take a look at my change order.

title: Introduction to Procore Viewpoint V
heading: Introduction to Procore_Viewpoint Vista Integration by ERP Team
text: This is just going to be additional scope to the original contract. And you’ll see right now that the "Send to ERP" button is not active—that’s just because we have to flip our status over here to approved. And once we do that, we can send it to ERP. In terms of our SOV on the contract, yeah, we’re using the same cost code, so we’re adding additional dollars to the same line item. We’ll also increase the contract value by $10,000. I’ll go ahead and click the "Send to ERP" button and jump over to our ERP tool, this time over to commitment change orders. And similar to what we saw previously, we’ve got our commitment change order here for that project. You can see the contract number.

title: Introduction to Procore Viewpoint V
heading: Introduction to Procore_Viewpoint Vista Integration by ERP Team
text: We’ll go ahead as the accounting approver, click "Accept," and we’ll go ahead and start the export process. Okay, we see that our change order has been successfully exported to Vista. And we’ll go ahead now back over to Vista. Again, I’m going to go ahead and run the SL Subcontract Ledger Report. And here we go, we’ll hop to subcontract 4, and what we can see now is we’ve got change order detail on this contract. And so the information came over from Procore—same date and month, we’ve got the description of added scope, we’ve got our additional cost of $10,000, and we can now see that the total contract amount, the new contract or current contract amount, is $60,000.

title: Introduction to Procore Viewpoint V
heading: Introduction to Procore_Viewpoint Vista Integration by ERP Team
text: Okay, so that’s it for the kind of short demo of the data transfer between the ERP system Viewpoint Vista and Procore. Each ERP connector, just to kind of get into it, has its whole list of support articles that will provide detail about which data connects between the two systems. From a very high-level overview, I’ll kind of bring that up here—down into like individual fields that map between the two systems. And this is all available on the Procore ERP support site. So once again, thanks for listening and hopefully that was informative. Thank you.

title: Acumatica vision ERP — FAQ
heading: Background
text: Your ERP integration often requires you to take specific actions in order to sync items like contracts, invoices, or change orders. With Procore's Acumatica® and MYOB Advanced Construction Connectors, there is no action required to sync your prime contract. However, certain conditions must be met for an automatic sync to be activated.

title: Acumatica vision ERP — FAQ
heading: Answer
text:
Prime contracts in Procore automatically sync to Acumatica® or MYOB Advanced Construction as a summarized single line item within the Revenue Budget tab. Your prime contract is automatically synced when the following conditions are met:

title: Acumatica vision ERP — FAQ
heading: Answer

title: Cmic ERP — FAQ
heading: Answer
text:
Procore was designed to allow users with the appropriate permissions to add new companies to their project's Directory. For every new company added to a project's Directory, a corresponding record is also created in the Company level Directory. This ensures that all company records that have been added to your projects are captured in the overarching Company level Directory. Additionally, when companies are invited to bid from the Procore Construction Network, the company is automatically added to your Company Directory as a 

A _connected company_ is a business or organization that is listed on theProcore Construction Network and added as a company in your Company level Directory tool.

title: Cmic ERP — FAQ
heading: Answer
text: While you can edit and maintain some of the business’s information in your Company level Directory, the business also has a public profile with information that they maintain. Connected Company. See What happens when companies and users are added from the Procore Construction Network to the Company Directory?

title: Cmic ERP — FAQ
heading: How Duplicated Company Entries Occur
text: When you add a new company record to a project's Directory tool, the system automatically adds that company record to the Company level Directory tool. If another user adds the same company to their project Directory with a small variation in spelling or abbreviation, both records will appear in the Company Directory.

title: Cmic ERP — FAQ
heading: How Duplicated Company Entries Occur
text:
##### Example

Jack, a project manager, added a new company record to Project A's Directory and named the company, 'Star Framing.'

Jane, also a project manager, added the same company to Project B's Directory, only she named the company, 'Star Framing, LLC.'

Since both project managers spelled the company name differently when creating the company record, the system created two (2) unique company records in your organization's Company level Directory tool.

title: Cmic ERP — FAQ
heading: How Duplicated Company Entries Occur
text:
One for 'Star Framing' and one for 'Star Framing, LLC.'

Preventing or consolidating duplicate entries ensures that all of the user, office, bidder, insurance, and change history information for the company is stored in a single record, instead of splitting data between two or more records. This ensures that your bid processes, insurance tracking, and reporting remain accurate. If you find duplicate company records in your system, follow the steps in Merge Companies to resolve the issue.

title: Cmic ERP — FAQ
heading: What if One of the companies is "Connected"?
text: Connected Companies are created when inviting companies to bid from the Procore Construction Network. At this time, you cannot merge Connected and unconnected companies into a single record. However, there are other ways that you can manage duplicates. See How are duplicate companies handled between the Directory tool and Procore Construction Network?

title: Cmic ERP — FAQ
heading: Important Note for Accounts Using ERP Integrations
text:
If your company's Procore account has been integrated with a third-party Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system, it is also possible to introduce duplicate entries when data in synced between your ERP system and Procore. When your Procore account is integrated with a third-party ERP system, it is very important to eliminate multiple entries from the Company Directory. This is because vendor records in the ERP system must share a direct link to its corresponding company entry in Procore. This one-to-one relationship (i.e., vendor-to-company) ensures data integrity between the two systems. For instructions, see:

 * Consolidate and Link ERP Companies to Procore Companies

title: Sage 300 cre ERP — FAQ
heading: Answer
text:
If you have added data (e.g., Budget, Change Orders, Commitments, Projects, and Vendors) to Procore and are ready to export that data to your integrated Sage 300 CRE system, a user will first send the data to the ERP Integrations tool for accounting acceptance. Next, an 

In Procore, an _Accounting Approver_ is an individual with the authority to accept and reject Procore data for export to an integrated ERP system. Accounting approvers can unlink several item types, such as commitments, commitment change orders, prime contract change orders, and subcontractor invoices, that have been synced between Procore and an integrated ERP system. See Which ERP Integrations are supported by Procore?

title: Sage 300 cre ERP — FAQ
heading: Answer
text: Accounting Approver reviews the data in the ERP Integrations tool and submits an 'Accept' response. This gives the system permission to begin the export process. When exporting Procore data to Sage 300 CRE, the system will validate the data that has been accepted for export to ensure that it does not conflict with any existing data in Sage. If the validation detects a potential issue, the system will display an error message to help you determine how to correct the issue so you can complete the export process.

title: Sage 300 cre ERP — FAQ

text:
* Commitments

 * Projects

 * Vendors

Sage ID is not unique; you tried to use a Sage ID for the commitment that's already been assigned to another commitment in your Sage 300 CRE system. The format of the specified Sage ID does not match your company's format. ##### Projects

 * **Job ID has already been taken**. When you see this message, check to see if the Sage Job ID that you entered is already in use. In this example, '03-015' was entered instead of '16-200'. * **Sage ID must be in the format: XX-XXX. This format can be edited in ERP Integration Settings**. When you see this message, check to see if the Sage Job ID that you entered is formatted properly. In this example, '16200' was entered instead of '16-200'.

 * **Vendor ID has already been taken**. When you see this error message, the 'Vendor ID' is already being used in your Sage 300 CRE system. In this example, the Vendor ID '100' was already assigned to a different 'Vendor' in Sage 300 CRE. You must enter a valid Vendor ID. ---

title: Sage 300 cre ERP — FAQ
heading: 9. Why is my Sage 300 CRE data not syncing? {#why-is-my-sage-300-cre-data-not-syncing}
text:
**Source URL:** https://v2.support.procore.com/faq-why-is-my-sage-data-not-syncing/ 
**Category:** Sage 300 CRE® ERP 
**Type:** Faq 
**Navigation:** Support Home > Why is my Sage 300 CRE data not syncing?

title: Sage 300 cre ERP — FAQ
heading: Answer
text:
There are a variety of reasons that may prevent your Procore and Sage 300 CRE® data from synchronizing properly. To diagnose the root cause of the issue, review the following possibilities:

 * Recent Changes are Missing in Procore

 * Restart the hh2 Services on the Sage 300 CRE® Server

 * Invalid Login Credentials (Between Procore and hh2)

 * Invalid Login Credentials (Between hh2 and Sage 300 CRE®)

 * Network Firewall: Access Denied

* * *

title: Sage 300 cre ERP — FAQ
heading: Recent Changes are Missing in Procore
text:
Although data is being synced as expected, a user may have added new to your Sage 300 CRE® after the system completed its last data sync. To address this issue, you have two options:

 * Wait for the next automatic sync to complete. To learn more about the sync schedule, see Configure the Sync Schedule for Sage 300 CRE®. OR

 * Manually sync your data. See Perform an On-Demand Sync with Sage 300 CRE®. * * *

title: Sage 300 cre ERP — FAQ
heading: Restart the hh2 Services on the Sage 300 CRE Server
text:
** _Recommended Fix_** : Ensure that the hh2 services are running. 1. Log into your company's Sage 300 CRE® server. _Note_ : If you do not have direct access to your Sage 300 CRE® server, you can Remote Desktop Connection. 2. Go to **Start** > **Computer** (right-click) > **Manage**. 3. Expand "Configuration" and click **Services**. 4. Scroll down the **Services** list and locate these hh2 services:

 * hh2 MongoDB Service

 * hh2 Synchronization Service

 5. Right-click and choose **Restart** from the shortcut menu. This manually restarts the selected hh2 service. _Note_ : It is recommended that you restart the hh2 synchronization service, even if the Status indicates that it is already started. * * *

title: Sage 300 cre ERP — FAQ
heading: Invalid Credentials (Between Procore and hh2)
text: The hh2 login credentials that Procore uses to access your account's data (from hh2 servers) is no longer valid. As a result, you cannot view any data under the Company level Integrations tool until its fixed. **_Recommended Fix_** : Contact your Procore point of contact and provide them with your hh2 credentials, you cannot change your hh2 credentials in Procore's web application. * * *

title: Sage 300 cre ERP — FAQ
heading: Invalid Login Credentials (Between hh2 and Sage 300 CRE)
text: The login credentials for the user profile that has hh2 used to access Sage 300 CRE® data is no longer valid. Check the Sage 300 CRE® user database to make sure that the user profile that the hh2 synchronization client uses to access your Sage 300 CRE® database still exists and has the appropriate permissions to access your Sage 300 CRE® database. Make sure the password was not changed or accidentally expired. The user must be a member of the 'Application' and 'Security' admin groups. **_Recommended Fix_** : Contact your Sage 300 CRE® Server Administrator and have them provide you with the correct login credentials for the "hh2" user. Change your hh2 login preferences in the hh2 synchronization client. * * *

title: Sage 300 cre ERP — FAQ
heading: Network Firewall: Access Denied
text: The network firewall permissions for the Sage 300 CRE® server may have changed. As a result, hh2 servers can no longer connect to the Sage 300 CRE® server. _Recommended Fix_ : Contact your Network Administrator, Sage 300 CRE® Server Administrator, or the company hosting your Sage 300 CRE® server to ensure that the firewall is configured to accept incoming requests from hh2 servers. ---

title: Yardi voyager ERP — FAQ

heading: Background
text: For ERP Connectors that offer transactional syncing, there can be occasional discrepancies in the values for Job Costs on a project.

title: Acumatica vision ERP — Tutorial
heading: Things to Consider
text:
* **Required User Permissions** :

 * 'Admin' on the Company Admin tool. * **Additional Information** :

 * To set up a budget view for real-time labor productivity, see Resource Tracking and Project Financials: Setup Guide. * To set up a labor productivity cost budget view, see Set Up the Procore Labor Productivity Cost Budget View. * Any user with 'Read Only' permission or higher on the Budget tool has access permission to apply the view to a project's budget. See Apply the View, Snapshot, Group, and Filter Options on a Budget or Forecasting View.

title: Acumatica vision ERP — Tutorial
heading: Things to Consider
text:
* For companies using the ERP Integrations tool: **Show/Hide**

 * If your company account is using the ERP Integrations tool, Procore automatically provides you with a budget view for your 

In Procore, the term _integrated ERP System_ , is used to refer to _Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP)_ software applications that can be configured to exchange data between Procore and a supported application using the Company level ERP Integrations tool. See Which ERP integrations are supported by Procore? Integrated ERP System. See Which ERP integrations are supported by Procore? for details about your specific ERP connector. * Any custom budget views that you create for an ERP Integration must contain all of the required ERP data columns.

title: Acumatica vision ERP — Tutorial
heading: Things to Consider
text:
This ensures that Procore can send the required budget data to the company's ERP Integrations tool for acceptance for export to the integrated ERP system by an 

In Procore, an _Accounting Approver_ is an individual with the authority to accept and reject Procore data for export to an integrated ERP system. Accounting approvers can unlink several item types, such as commitments, commitment change orders, prime contract change orders, and subcontractor invoices, that have been synced between Procore and an integrated ERP system. See Which ERP Integrations are supported by Procore? Accounting Approver. See Send a Budget to ERP Integrations for Accounting Acceptance.

title: Acumatica vision ERP — Tutorial
heading: Create a new Budget View
text:
1. Navigate to the company's **Admin** tool. 2. Under 'Tool Settings', click **Budget**. ##### Tip

**Did you know you can also launch the 'Budget Views' page directly from the project's Budget tool?** A Procore Administrator can open the 'Budget Views' page in the Company Admin tool directly from a project's budget. To do this, maximize the right sidebar in the Budget tool when viewing the 'Budget' tab. Under the 'Configurations' section, click the **Configure Budgeting Views** link. * Click **Set Up New Budget View**. * In the **Setup a New Budget** window, select the **Procore ERP Direct Cost Budget** and click **Create. **

* Click **Configure Columns.**

title: Acumatica vision ERP — Tutorial
heading: Create a Source Column to display transactional Job Cost values in:
text:
1. Click **Create Source Column.**

 2. Configure the New Source column. * Enter 'Transactional Job Costs' in the **Column Name** field. * Select **Direct Costs** in the **Column Source** field. 3. Select the following filters:

 * **Type.** Add checkmarks to the boxes next to the following item types:

 * **Invoice**

 * **Expense**

 * **Payroll**

 * **Subcontractor Invoices**

 * **Status.** Add a checkmark to the **Approved** status. * Click **Save** to save your source column configuration.

title: Acumatica vision ERP — Tutorial
heading: Create a Source Column to display ERP Job Cost values in:
text:
1. Click **Create Source Column.**

 2. Configure the New Source column. * Enter ERP Job Costs in the **Column Name** field. * Select **ERP Job Costs** in the **Column Source** field. 3. Click **Save** to save your source column configuration.

title: Acumatica vision ERP — Tutorial
heading: Create a Calculated Column to determine the variance:
text:
1. Click **Create Calculated Column.**

 2. Configure the **New Formula** column: 

 * Enter 'Variance' in the **Column Name** field. * Select **Currency** in the **Format** drop-down menu. * In the first **Pick a Column** drop-down menu, select **ERP Job Costs.**

 * Select **Subtract (-)** from the Operations drop-down menu. * In the second **Pick a Column** drop-down menu, select **Transactional Job Costs**. * Click **Save** to save the new calculated column. After closing the Configure Columns window, the system returns you to the new budget view's window, where you can preview the new view and assign it to your projects. **Assign to Projects.** Place a checkmark next to the desired projects in the drop-down menu.

title: Acumatica vision ERP — Tutorial
heading: Create a Calculated Column to determine the variance:
text: **Preview with Project.** Select a project from the drop-down menu to preview with the new view applied. In the Preview, the newly created columns will appear to the right of the table. If you find any unexpected variance(s), to confirm the steps to resolve. ---

* **Required User Permissions** :

 * Only available if you have the synced job cost transactions feature enabled. * Editing or deleting direct cost transactions can cause the costs in the Procore project and the synced ERP project to no longer match. * If the synced direct cost transaction data is ever re-synced from your ERP integration, any updates you've made will be overwritten.

title: Acumatica vision ERP — Tutorial
heading: Steps
text:
1. Go to the **Company level ERP Integrations** tool. 2. Click **Configure Settings** . 3. Go to **General Settings**. 4. Mark the **Edit Synced Direct Cost Transactions** checkbox. * This setting will allow you to edit or delete direct cost transactions synced with your ERP system. * These updates will NOT sync back to your ERP system and once a change has been made, it can't be undone. * Edits to synced costs will be available to review in the synced item's change history. 5. Click **Update.**

**Category:** Acumatica Vision ERP

title: Acumatica vision ERP — Tutorial
heading: Background
text:
In most cases, to sync an item to your ERP system, the item must first be accepted or rejected for export by an accounting approver in the Company level ERP tool. When enabled, the Direct Export feature allows you to configure your ERP integration to bypass the accounting approver step when sending Commitments, CCOs, and Invoices to ERP. If this feature was previously enabled, it can also be disabled. If disabled, items that were synced while the feature was enabled can then be managed through the Company level ERP Integrations tool by an accounting approver. ##### Tip

You can use the Workflows tool instead of the accounting approver step to manage the approval flow of an item that is sent to ERP.

title: Acumatica vision ERP — Tutorial
heading: Background
text:
The following three (3) configuration options are available with this feature:

 * **Direct Export disabled (default)**. You can keep using your integration the same way with no changes. * **Direct Export enabled, workflows NOT applied**. When enabled without applying a workflow to the approval process for a Commitment, CCO, and/or Invoice, this feature simply allows these objects to be exported directly to your ERP system when clicking the 'Send to ERP' button on the item in its Project level tool. No approval in the Company level ERP integrations tool is required. * **Direct Export enabled, workflows applied**.

title: Acumatica vision ERP — Tutorial
heading: Background
text: You can enable the Direct Export feature, and choose to use a workflow for the ERP approval process prior to the 'Send to ERP' step, instead of approving an item for export through the Company level ERP Integrations tool. To learn about Procore's v2 Workflows tool (in Beta), including how to create workflow templates and assign them to projects, see Workflows. ---

title: Cmic ERP — Tutorial
heading: Background
text: During a construction project, you will often create prime contract change orders. When a PCCO is created in Procore, you might need to export it as an OCO to CMiC. Follow the steps below to export a Procore PCCO as an OCO to CMiC.

title: Cmic ERP — Tutorial
heading: Things to Consider
text:
* **Required User Permissions:**

 * _To enable the ‘Create Owner Change Orders’ setting,_ 'Admin' level permissions on the project's Admin tool. * _To submit a request to enable the feature in your company's Procore account,_ you must be your company's Procore Administrator or the CMiC integration contact on your company's Procore account. * **Requirements:**

 * Your company's Procore Administrator must submit a request to your company's Procore point of contact to enable this feature on the backend of Procore. * A user with 'Admin' permission on the project's Admin tool must enable the capability to create owner change orders as described in the steps below.

title: Cmic ERP — Tutorial
heading: Things to Consider
text:
* **Additional Information:**

 * Not all ERP Integrations support the creation of owner change orders.

title: Cmic ERP — Tutorial
heading: Steps
text: 1. Navigate to the project's **Admin** tool. 2. Under 'Project Settings', click **General**. 3. Scroll to 'Advanced'. 4. Mark the checkbox to **Create Owner Change Orders**. 5. Click **Update**. 6. Complete the steps in Export a PCCO to ERP. ---

title: Jobpac ERP — Tutorial
heading: Background
text: Cost codes need to be added to a project for use with Procore's financial tools, and your ERP integration.

title: Jobpac ERP — Tutorial
heading: Things to Consider
text:
* **Required User Permissions** :

 * _To add or edit project cost codes_ , 'Admin' on the project's Admin tool. OR

 * _To add or edit project cost codes as a user with 'Standard' or 'Read Only' level permission to the project's Admin tool_ , the 'Manage Cost Codes' granular permission must be enabled on the permission template associated with your user account on the project. See Grant Granular Permissions in a Project Permissions Template.

title: Jobpac ERP — Tutorial
heading: Steps
text:
1. Navigate to the Project level **Admin** tool. 2. Under 'Project Settings', click the **Work Breakdown Structure** link. 3. In the 'Segments' list, click the **Cost Codes** link. 4. Click **Cost Codes from Company**. 5. In the 'Add Cost Codes to this Project' window, choose from these options: 
 
 

 * To copy all company cost codes to the project, click **Select All**. * To select specific cost codes, type a code in the **Search Cost Codes** box and highlight the codes to add. * To choose cost codes, expand the desired segment items and highlight the segment items to copy. 6. Click **Add**. ---

title: Netsuite ERP — Tutorial
heading: Background
text:
Company level WBS codes are pulled down onto a project in Procore. Each full WBS code on the project (cost code, cost type, custom segment) will be synced to NetSuite® as an **Item**. The syncing of new WBS codes at the project level code is triggered in the following ways:

 * The WBS Code is used on a Subcontractor Invoice that is synced to NetSuite®. * The WBS Code is added to the Procore Budget and a manual Cost Code Sync is run. ##### Note

title: Netsuite ERP — Tutorial

text:

title: Quickbooks desktop ERP — Tutorial
heading: Background
text:
If your company is collecting timecard entries with Procore's Timesheets tool and processing your payroll with QuickBooks® Desktop, you can export that data from Procore and import it into QuickBooks® Desktop. However, before you can export that data from Procore, you first need to perform a few set up steps. This tutorial describes the first step in the setup process—exporting a preformatted Intuit Interchange Format (IIF) file from the QuickBooks® Desktop system where you intend to transfer your Procore time entry data. ##### Notes

 * The IIF file provides the data structure that Procore needs to ensure that transferred data is formatted as required in QuickBooks®.

title: Quickbooks desktop ERP — Tutorial
heading: Background
text:
Your IIF file must match this structure:

 * Cost Codes Numbering

 * Cost Codes Format

 * Time Types (QuickBooks® Payroll Item)

 * Employee Names

 * Customer Names

 * Job Names

 * Technical support or assistance for creating or importing an Intuit Interchange Format (IIF) file is NOT provided. It is recommended that you always create a backup of your IIF file in case you need to reference it later. * Transferring time entries from Procore is a separate function and does NOT require the Procore + QuickBooks® Connector. ---
